prediction.likelyOutcome: Navient should recover its conceded $503,822.72 cooling tower claim in full, and BPG's counterclaim should be substantially reduced from its $817,845 ask — most sharply on the rooftop air units (where BPG's own witness conceded a $8,400 repair fix instead of $240,000 replacement) and the transformer (a strong SOL defense plus a weak betterment-style damages theory). The heat pump dispute is the closest call and could go either toward the ~$135,850 non-operational-unit figure or, less likely, closer to BPG's full $434,500 age-based theory. Netting it out, Navient likely walks away with a judgment in the roughly $200,000–$420,000 range in its favor, before any fee award under the lease's prevailing-party clause.

issues.label: Transformer Counterclaim / Statute of Limitations Defense

outcome.description: The Superior Court entered post-trial judgment for Navient in $503,822.72 (the conceded cooling-tower reimbursement) less $79,650 awarded to BPG on its counterclaim ($71,250 to repair 25 non-operational heat pumps and $8,400 to repair two rooftop air units), a net principal of $424,172.72 plus prejudgment interest from March 17, 2020; BPG's transformer and elevator claims failed. Navient was held the prevailing party entitled to its attorneys' fees and expenses under lease section 28(q) (amount not stated). This is the trial-level decision; no appeal is reflected in the source.
